events.title: Thomas More resigns as Lord Chancellor
events.description: A day after the clergy submitted to Henry VIII's authority, Sir Thomas More gave up the Great Seal. His refusal to accept the king's supremacy over the Church led to his execution in 1535.
events.html: A day after the clergy submitted to Henry VIII's authority, Sir Thomas More gave up the Great Seal. His refusal to accept the king's supremacy over the Church led to his execution in 1535.

events.title: Marie Antoinette marries the future Louis XVI
events.description: The fourteen-year-old Austrian archduchess married the French dauphin at Versailles, sealing an alliance between Habsburgs and Bourbons. Both were guillotined during the Revolution.
events.html: The fourteen-year-old Austrian archduchess married the French dauphin at Versailles, sealing an alliance between Habsburgs and Bourbons. Both were guillotined during the Revolution.

events.title: Andrew Johnson escapes conviction by one vote
events.description: The Senate voted 35 to 19 to convict President Johnson on the first article tried, one vote short of the two-thirds needed. Johnson was the first US president to be impeached.
events.html: The Senate voted 35 to 19 to convict President Johnson on the first article tried, one vote short of the two-thirds needed. Johnson was the first US president to be impeached.

events.title: First Academy Awards are presented in Hollywood
events.description: About 270 guests attended a dinner at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel where the first Oscars were handed out in around fifteen minutes. Wings won the top prize.
events.html: About 270 guests attended a dinner at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel where the first Oscars were handed out in around fifteen minutes. Wings won the top prize.

events.title: Theodore Maiman operates the first laser
events.description: At Hughes Research Laboratories in California, Maiman produced a pulse of red laser light from a ruby crystal. Lasers went on to transform medicine, communications and industry.
